newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia tightens tax laws on asset sales.
newsitem.headline: Australia tightens tax laws on asset sales.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello on Monday announced a tightening of tax laws relating to the sale of assets by tax exempt organisations.

"Under existing taxation legislation, taxpayers who acquire the depreciable assets of tax exempt entities receive different taxation treatment depending on how the sale is structured," Costello said in a statement.

"Currently, where a tax exempt entity is sold, depreciable assets held within that entity are depreciated for taxation purposes on the basis of their notional writedown value," he said. "These rules can be circumvented by carving out the assets
of the entity for separate sale so that the purchaser claims depreciation on the basis of the purchase price," he said.
"These circumstances provide scope for parties to the sale to structure arrangements to gain significant taxation advantages," Costello said.

Costello said that from Monday in all sales of depreciable assets by exempt organisations associated with the sale of a business the buyer would get the same opening value for tax depreciation, regardless of how the sale was structured.
The government balanced the aims of a fair price for the seller, certainty, administrative ease and consistency, he said.

"The government has therefore decided to legislate to only allow the purchasers of exempt entities, or assets owned by exempt entities, to claim depreciation based on the higher of notional writedown value and a pre-existing audited book value recorded in the exempt entities' audited annual account," Costello said. "This gives the purchaser the option to choose the most beneficial valuation," he said.
